chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd al-Yaqtini, from Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn Marwak al-Ta'i, from Abu Abdillah, from his forefathers (peace be upon them).

He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Which bond of faith is the strongest?' They said: 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' Some of them said: 'Prayer,' and some said: 'Alms-tax,' and some said: 'Fasting,' and some said: 'Pilgrimage and Visitation,' and some said: 'Striving.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'For all that you have mentioned there is merit, but it is not that; rather, the strongest bond of faith is loving for the sake of Allah, hating for the sake of Allah, taking the allies of Allah as allies, and disassociating from the enemies of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He.'

key_terms.التَّبَرِّي مِنْ أَعْدَاءِ اللَّهِ: disassociating from the enemies of Allah
key_terms.الْبُغْضُ فِي اللَّهِ: hating for the sake of Allah
key_terms.الْحُبُّ فِي اللَّهِ: loving for the sake of Allah
key_terms.تَوَلَّى أَوْلِيَاءَ اللَّهِ: taking the allies of Allah as allies

ai.seo_question: What is considered the strongest bond of faith in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Mani al-Akhbar*, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) elevates *al-wala' wa al-bar'a* (loyalty and disassociation) as the 'strongest bond of faith' (*awthar al-iman*), distinguishing it from the pillars of worship which, while virtuous, are secondary to this theological foundation. This concept is central to Shia scholarship, particularly in defining the spiritual identity of the faithful through their connection to the Ahl al-Bayt and their distinctiveness from opponents. It underscores that true faith is not merely ritualistic but rooted in a profound, relational alignment with divine love and enmity.

en.basel-kadem: 54. We were told by Muhammed bin Musa bin Mutawakkil, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Yahya al-‘Attar, from Ahmad bin Muhammed bin Isa, from Uthman bin Isa, from Abu Ayub, the silk maker, that he said: I heard Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, say: When this verse was sent down unto the Prophet, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family: «The one who brings a good deed, will have better than it» [27:89] the Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, said: O Allah, increase me.

Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, then sent down unto him: «Who is it who will loan to Allah a good loan, so that He may multiply it to him many times over?» [2:245] The Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, then knew that abundance from Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, cannot be counted and has no end.
